How these numbers are worked out
How these numbers are worked out
"Full speed" is what the buildings would do if they never stopped. It comes straight from their recipe.
"Right now" comes from the game's own timers: it records how long each machine spends working, and that share is applied to its recipe. Averaged over the last 12 months.

Rainwater harvesters have no such timer. They follow the game's own formula: effective rainy days per year, times the daily collection, divided by 12 months. That is around 42 rainy days a year on a normal game. Being a yearly average, a drought or a storm will give something else.
Farms and the generators that burn a product, such as the diesel generator, keep no timers either. Only their capacity is shown, and the warnings above name the ones found in your selection.
Electricity compares two capacities: what the buildings draw at full speed against what the generators in the area could put out. Solar panels count at their peak, which they only reach in full sun.
